question: What claim about the nature of languages arises from the distinction between those heard and those unheard in this context?
premises: Languages of varied forms are present as a distinct class.
Some of these languages fall into the class of the heard.
Some of these languages fall into the class of the unheard.
inference: Languages of varied forms comprise both heard and unheard kinds.
plain_english: Languages of varied forms indeed arise, both heard and unheard.
